actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: TDW-MAT extends the ThreeDWorld Transport Challenge into a multi-agent setting on top of the TDW platform
The environment class is TDW, a subclass of the legacy Gym Env
gym id transport_challenge_MA is registered with entry point tdw_gym:TDW
The single-agent action space is a Dict of type Discrete(7), object Discrete(30), arm Discrete(2) and a message Text of at most 1000 characters

The action type 0 moves forward 0.5 m, 1 turns left 15 degrees, 2 turns right 15 degrees, 3 reaches for and grasps, 4 puts in a container, 5 drops and 6 sends a message; every other type asserts False

The single-agent observation space declares rgb (3, screen_size, screen_size), seg_mask (screen_size, screen_size, 3), depth (screen_size, screen_size), an agent pose Box(-30, 30, (6,)), two hand slots, 50 visible-object slots, status Discrete(4), valid Discrete(2), FOV Box(0, 120, (1,)), a 4x4 camera matrix, two message slots and current_frames Discrete(30)
action_space is built from observation_space_single, not from action_space_single: each agent id maps to the observation space
step compares action['arm'] with the strings left and right before it reaches the controller, while the declared arm space is Discrete(2)
reset takes keyword-only seed, options and output_dir; options must carry scene and layout and reset raises ValueError without it
reset launches the external ThreeDWorld build through TransportChallenge with launch_build
reset calls super().reset(seed=seed) and creates np.random.RandomState(seed) for the episode's randomness
step returns the legacy four-tuple (observation, reward, done, info)
reset returns (observation, info, env_api), a three-tuple
reward is reduced by 0.1 for each agent whose action status is neither success nor ongoing
done becomes True when num_frames reaches max_frame or the goal is achieved
screen_size is a constructor parameter with default 512 and max_frames has default 3000
reset opens ./dataset/room_types.json from the working directory
reset opens ./dataset/name_map.json from the working directory
TDW-MAT pins tdw==1.11.23.5
The setup uses Python 3.9 and an editable install
The transport challenge asset bundles must be downloaded and unzipped under TDW_MAT

determinism.notes: reset(seed=...) fixes the fake's object placement and the action sequence repeats a trajectory; upstream seeds np.random.RandomState(seed) at reset (tdw_gym.py:229). The fake draws with Python's random.Random, not numpy's generator, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two implementations

fidelity.engine: gymnasium:transport_challenge_MA (reduced analytic stand-in; upstream is ThreeDWorld)
gaps: no physics and no contacts: the fake is an analytic F0 stand-in that moves a point agent and tracks held object ids; the upstream environment advances the ThreeDWorld engine

no fixed timestep: one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one upstream action decision, and the upstream controller advances a variable number of frames per action (info['num_frames_for_step'], tdw_gym.py:748); fidelity.timestep_ms is 0

the fake returns 2x2 images (rgb 3x2x2, seg_mask 2x2x3, depth 2x2) instead of the upstream 3 x screen_size x screen_size, screen_size x screen_size x 3 and screen_size x screen_size arrays (screen_size defaults to 512, tdw_gym.py:52), and its visible-object slots, camera matrix and object ids are placeholders; empty object and hand slots use -1, outside the declared Discrete range, because the bridge needs an integer where upstream pads with None

the fake accepts a seed-only reset and supplies a placeholder scene; upstream reset requires options with scene and layout (tdw_gym.py:227) and reads ./dataset/name_map.json and ./dataset/room_types.json from the working directory

the fake corrects the action space: the contract is the declared single-agent action_space_single, while upstream builds action_space from observation_space_single (tdw_gym.py:139-140) and its step compares a string arm, not the declared Discrete(2) index (tdw_gym.py:624-627); the fake serves the default one-agent configuration and wraps the action under agent id 0 for TDW.step's agent map
the fake uses Python random.Random, upstream uses numpy's np.random.RandomState; one seed gives different trajectories on the two
the declared action field message is a Text space, which the bridge has no string kind for, so its published schema is an open object; the fake accepts a string and uses it for action type 6
no rendering, no top-down images and no assets: the TDW build, the X server and the transport challenge asset bundles are not present

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
